s: External capabilities that AI agents can invoke to interact with the real world - APIs, databases, code interpreters, file systems, and other services beyond the LLM's native text generation.
w: Tools extend LLM capabilities beyond text generation. Each tool has a schema definition (name, description, parameters, return type) that the LLM uses to decide when and how to invoke it. The tool execution layer handles authentication, input validation, API calls, error handling, and result formatting. Tools can be stateful (maintaining connections to external services) or stateless (pure function transforms). Security policies restrict which tools agents can access and what parameters are permitted.
use: Agents needing to query live data (search APIs, databases, file systems)
Code execution and data analysis within agent workflows
External API calls for real-world actions (sending emails, making purchases)
Retrieval-augmented generation combining search with LLM reasoning
avoid: Tasks that can be solved with pure LLM reasoning (tool calls add latency and failure modes)
Frequently changing external APIs without versioned tool definitions
Tools with unpredictable latency that can blow through agent time budgets

props.timeout_ms: Maximum execution time before tool call is abandoned
props.permission_level: Scope of actions the tool is authorized to perform

pat.d: Define tools as JSON schemas, let LLM select tool + parameters from schema, validate output before returning to agent.
Track tool failure rates, temporarily disable tools that exceed failure thresholds to prevent cascading failures.

pits: Overly permissive tool schemas allowing agents to perform destructive actions
Missing tool result size limits causing context window overflow
Tool hallucination where LLM invents parameters not in the schema
Unbounded tool call loops where agent repeatedly calls failing tools
tips: Keep tool descriptions concise but precise - the LLM uses them for selection decisions
Implement sandboxed execution for code interpreter tools to prevent system compromise
Return structured (not free-text) results from tools for reliable downstream processing
